clue.text: A man of the church needing little rest maybe

parts.note: mini means little, as in a mini skirt

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word rest could be in some other form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman so busy he hardly gets a moment's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal, applied to 'rest'; 'little' gives the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchman who serves a congregation is a pastor or clergyman by that title.

clue.text: Stylish doctor accompanied by a beautiful girl

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A fashionable doctor seen out with a pretty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean fashionable, in the current style.

clue.text: Mentioning worry about many inside

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the word for worry encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
in means inside

explanation.surface: Bringing up the worry that many are trapped indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention someone is to cite them by name.

clue.text: A woman in consequence turned in an article

parts.note: so means therefore, in consequence

indicators.note: turned signals the little word in is flipped round

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Consequently a woman handed in a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female first name, so any woman so called.

clue.text: A schoolboy's tie on an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil wears his tie in an odd, unconventional way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; Eton is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at Eton College, the English boarding school, is known by this name.

clue.text: Bound to follow severe weather

definitions.meaning: a bound is a leap or jump
the season that comes after winter

explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a leap, and spring is the season that follows harsh wintry weather.

clue.text: Leisure interest of a Greek character in recent times

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means in recent times

explanation.surface: A Greek man has lately taken up a new hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is a popular hobby, a leisure pursuit.

clue.text: One way rental can be settled for home

parts.note: in is one direction, the opposite of out

indicators.note: settled suggests putting the letters of rental in order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Agreeing a one-way rental deal for a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be settled' rearranges 'rental'. 'home' is used as in home affairs or the Home Office: domestic, not foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: Home affairs are domestic ones, inside the country rather than abroad.

clue.text: Jersey is of course among the Channel Islands

definitions.meaning: a jersey is a knitted sweater, also called by this island's name

definitions.text: of course among the Channel Islands
definitions.meaning: naturally it is one of the islands near Jersey

explanation.definitionFit: A guernsey is a woollen sweater like a jersey, and Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands off France.

clue.text: Act before an underling gains control

indicators.note: before places the word for act ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to do is to act
a minion is a servile underling

explanation.surface: A subordinate takes charge after acting first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is rule or sovereignty over territory or people.

clue.text: Left on the wagon in a French island in short

indicators.note: in places the teetotal letters within the French word

parts.note: ile is French for island
TT is teetotal, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone left sober on a small island in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Small or brief, both mean not long or not great in size.

clue.text: Break for a game

definitions.meaning: a card game in which matching cards are called out

explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break cleanly, and snap is a children's card game.

clue.text: Issue about a stein being broken-it'sascandal

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for issue encloses the rest

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: broken shows the letters of a stein are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A beer mug gets smashed and someone calls it a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broken' rearranges 'a stein', and 'about' puts the word for issue around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal causes a stir or furore, a public sensation.

clue.text: Protection for the domestic worker

parts.note: the garment a cook or cleaner ties on to keep clothes clean

explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore-like garment worn over clothes to protect them from mess.

clue.text: Some of the most unyielding persons can be overcome

indicators.note: some of means only part of the words is used, so the letters lurk inside them

explanation.surface: Even the toughest people can sometimes be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stunned is to be dazed or overwhelmed.

clue.text: Places specialising in skin-treatment

parts.note: reads like beauty clinics, but means works where hides become leather

explanation.definitionFit: Works where animal hides are cured into leather.

clue.text: 1 across will be given report by coppers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the coins come beside the word for report

parts.note: P is penny, the copper coin
to relate is to report or tell

explanation.surface: A clergyman will be given a report by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' points to the answer of 1 across, a clergyman; 'coppers' looks like police but means pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other senior churchman is a high-ranking clergyman.

clue.text: A patient individual may well be glad about a salary-increase

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the pay rise
may well be suggests glad becomes something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: a rise is an increase in salary

explanation.surface: Someone might be pleased to get a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' rearranges 'glad', which wraps the pay rise. Griselda is the patient wife of medieval legend, told by Chaucer and Boccaccio.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient Griselda is the byword for long-suffering wifely endurance in Chaucer and Boccaccio.

clue.text: Odds on key service

parts.note: evens is betting odds of one to one
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Betting at even money on a crucial outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer is the Anglican church's sung evening worship.

clue.text: Deplore having to accept steady income

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the word for deplore takes in the next piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret or deplore
even means steady or regular

explanation.surface: Regretting the need to make do on a fixed income.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, earnings.

clue.text: Simple midshipman

definitions.meaning: Mr Midshipman ... is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel

explanation.definitionFit: Easy means not difficult, and Midshipman Easy is the title character of a Marryat novel.

clue.text: Lights for swimmers

explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light and also flat cartilaginous fish.

clue.text: Telephone about a point the Spanish find staggering

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the telephone word encloses the rest

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
E is East, a compass point
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Phoning around for a Spanish answer leaves one baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling is lurching or tottering, as if dizzy.

clue.text: Heartless people returning fish and other food

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters are removed, leaving the first and last
returning means the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: Cruel people bringing back fish and other things to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundnut is a food, different from the fish named before.

clue.text: Cuts odious creatures in a seagoing vessel

indicators.note: in places the creatures inside the vessel

parts.note: SS is steamship
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A ship cuts out its nasty vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice is to cut thin pieces.

clue.text: Get an impression of sound thinking

explanation.definitionFit: To sense is to perceive something, and sense is sound judgment.

clue.text: Pretty plant becoming dreadful weed in time

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the period

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters of weed are in a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovely flower turns into an awful weed over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges 'weed', set inside the word for a period; speedwell is a small blue wildflower.

clue.text: Drank up the store

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so toped means drank

explanation.surface: Someone drank everything in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse.

clue.text: Visit a joint without approval

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the joint surrounds the approval

parts.note: a loin is a joint of meat
OK is approval

explanation.surface: Calling on someone with a joint of meat that nobody approved.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief call on someone, a short visit.

clue.text: A man's overwhelming fear of a certain area of Europe

definitions.text: of a certain area of Europe

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
panic is sudden overwhelming fear

explanation.surface: One man's terror of a certain part of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Spain and the Iberian region.

clue.text: Impressive, but only for a few weeks

definitions.text: but only for a few weeks
definitions.meaning: a month lasts only some four weeks

explanation.definitionFit: August means stately, and August is the summer month of four or so weeks.

clue.text: A stage presentation-it creates quite a stir

indicators.note: a presentation is a staging of something, here the letters are put on in new order

explanation.surface: A theatre production that causes a real stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitating is stirring things up, causing a commotion.
